title: Independence of Dai Viet (Battle of Bach Dang, 938)
summary: In 938 the Vietnamese leader Ngo Quyen defeated a Chinese force at the Bach Dang River estuary near Haiphong and proclaimed an independent Vietnam. The victory ended the Chinese political rule over the north that had begun when the Han emperor Wudi conquered Nan Yue around 111 BCE. Independent Vietnamese dynasties followed; under the Ly from 1010 the state was called Dai Viet. The same estuary saw further battles against China in 981 and 1288.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopedia.com and INA give 938; Columbia AFE gives 939.

where.modern_name: Bach Dang River, near Hai Phong, Vietnam
where.historical_name: Bach Dang River (Song Bach Dang), Tinh Hai quan (northern Vietnam)

importance.justification: Ended about a thousand years of Chinese rule in northern Vietnam and began its lasting independence (R2 D3 T4 L3).

related.because: Han Wudi's conquest of Nanyue in 111 BCE established Chinese imperial administration over the Red River delta, which the victory at Bach Dang in 938 brought to an end.
Columbia AFE notes that the Tang set up the Protectorate of An Nan over northern Vietnam before Ngo Quyen ended Chinese rule.
